turns.q: Honestly, is the pricier one worth the extra, or is the cheaper one fine?
turns.replyTail: , I can’t say the pricier option is worth it based on price alone. Invisalign costs and coverage can vary, and dental insurance may cover a percentage or set amount up to a lifetime orthodontic maximum. The cheaper option may be fine if it addresses your doctor’s recommended treatment needs; the higher-priced option may be worthwhile only if it includes treatment or refinements you actually need. Comparing the two written treatment plans and total out-of-pocket costs is the safest way to decide.
